questions.evidenceQuote: A bit of history first. In 1936, psychologists Gordon W. Allport and Henry S. Odbert set out to identify all the words describing personality or personal behavior in Webster’s 1925 New International Dictionary. That dictionary contained roughly 400,000 entries, of which they found 17,953 personal descriptors, or 4.5 percent of the English vocabulary recorded there. Personality is often defined as characteristic patterns of thinking, feeling, and behavior, so the researchers removed all the words about temporary states, such as “frantic” and “rejoicing.”

specificFindings: Capitalised AND denotes intersection of all three life qualities. Pairwise counts can include the two triple-overlap people; source page54 Venn diagram and page55 continuation were visually checked.

The earlier sentence prints ten rich-and-meaningful people; the later page56 paragraph prints eight. Each source wording and local context is retained, without silently harmonising numbers or inventing an unprinted exclusive-only qualifier.

New York Times profiles tend to feature extraordinary individuals and are not representative of the general population. That said signals this limitation, not fabricated results or absent life information.
Checking reliable ratings before analysis is distinct from representative sampling or uniform article length. The local newspaper comparison concerns profiled people, not all Virginia residents.
Were perceived and rated refer to third-party text-based judgements. It could be keeps the less-adventurous explanation tentative; the shorter-obituary alternative is not dismissed.
Local happy66/56.9% and meaningful96/82.8% are parallel category findings. Likewise does not establish identical membership or mutually exclusive groups.
Mainly Americans motivates extension outside the United States, without claiming no foreign person ever appeared in those newspapers.

Actual page55 prints111 Straits Times obituaries, Forty and34.5%; these do not consistently convert. Full inherited translation already notes the mismatch. Questions retain the printed count/comparison, explicitly avoid deriving a new denominator or inventing a corrected number.
Straits Times happy25/21.6% and meaningful65/56.5% are retained as printed, with the original numeric caution. No national prevalence or random assignment is inferred.

Goldmund is a literary illustration and probably is preserved; he is not labeled an actually rated obituary subject. Jobs is a real-life illustration, not automatically a member of the specific2016 sample.
Alienated describes estranged relationships, not overseas relocation or medical diagnosis. Many is not all, and might not happy is not certain unhappiness in every moment.
Distinct dimensions may coexist: Gopnik and Linda provide the immediate context. Distinct is not mutually exclusive or proof that exploration requires lacking meaning.
The personality question opens a new inquiry; teaching an introductory course explains readiness for a brief Big Five introduction, not a claim to replace evidence with personal authority.

1936 is the research start and1925 the dictionary edition. The17,953 descriptors and approximately400,000 entries concern vocabulary recorded in that dictionary, not population frequency or all English across time.
